children: Wells Fargo cut its year-end S&P 500 (
target to 7,700 from 7,950, saying the index has limited upside from current levels and could fall 5%-10% first as the market enters the late innings of the earnings cycle.

Analyst Ohsung Kwon said the team has turned more cautious heading into September even as it raised its earnings forecasts to $425 for 2027 and $460 for 2028. Wells Fargo expects multiple compression to offset some of that earnings strength.
One of the biggest concerns is investor allocation. Kwon estimates equities now account for 72% of portfolios versus fixed income, the highest level since 1969. With the 10-year Treasury yield
nearing 5%, the firm calculates a fair equity allocation of roughly 60%, leaving a 12-percentage-point gap between actual and fair exposure.

That gap is the widest since 1969 and exceeds the level seen during the tech bubble. Historically, the spread has had a strong relationship with forward five-year equity excess returns, suggesting relatively limited upside from stocks versus bonds from here.
The firm also changed its sector stance, downgrading Technology
to Equal Weight from Overweight while upgrading Health Care
Within Technology, Kwon continues to prefer Software

. He sees political pushback against datacenter development as a growing risk and also flagged the stronger Korean won as a potential headwind for Samsung and SK Hynix, which could weigh on the broader memory trade. Kwon expects semiconductors to at least retest their July lows.

Health Care, by contrast, could benefit from a more defensive market backdrop. Wells Fargo also sees a potential Democratic sweep in the midterms as a positive for the sector, particularly if enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies are restored.
